subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but choosing how much cross-session process visibility and termination power to expose is a product and security boundary decision that automation should not invent.

options.title: Add guarded session exec controls
options.body: Create new additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and child/PTY/sandbox fallback tests.

options.title: Extend existing abort with opt-in kill
options.body: Add explicit kill-exec flags to existing session abort semantics while preserving current default behavior and documenting upgrade expectations.

options.title: Defer to narrower lifecycle work
options.body: Keep only the current agent-scoped process tool and subagent kill surfaces while related orphan/restart cleanup issues settle the underlying process ownership model.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec controls
recommendation.body: Create new additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and child/PTY/sandbox fallback tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current source-history signal across the Gateway session catalog, abort schema/handler, process supervisor, and process-tool code paths.
